turns.text: And I'd… practice my true response, right?
turns.zh: 然后我会……练习我真实的回应，对吧？

turns.text: My, I shouldn't say true… my gut response because sometimes just playing it out loud helps to get it out.
turns.zh: 我的，我不该说真实的……我的直觉反应，因为有时候只是大声说出来就有助于把它释放出来。

turns.text: But then when you put your, your first gut reaction out there for the world to see and hear, and then you look at it for a minute and you go, “Oh, well, that's not even how I really feel,” you know.
turns.zh: 但然后当你把你最初的直觉反应放到全世界面前去看去听，然后你看它一分钟，你说，‘哦，好吧，那甚至不是我真正的感受，’你知道吧。

turns.text: And what's going to be the outcome?
You know, there's going to be half the country that won't even hear the rest of the solution, if I start there.
turns.zh: 你知道，如果我从那里开始，会有半个国家甚至听不到解决方案的其余部分。

turns.text: If I start with my rage and anger, all I will do is play out my rage and anger, but I won't be able to effect any change.
turns.zh: 如果我以我的愤怒和怒火开始，我所做的只是发泄我的愤怒和怒火，但我无法带来任何改变。

turns.text: “Going high” is about the ultimate goal of “where we trying to go and what's the best way to get there.” And over the course of history, especially the history of civil rights, there was the rage, but there was always the plan.
turns.zh: “走高”是关于‘我们要去哪里以及到达那里的最佳方式是什么’的最终目标。在历史进程中，尤其是民权运动的历史中，有愤怒，但总是有计划。

turns.text: You know, the March on Washington was the cherry on top, after decades of legislative action and strategic sit downs.
turns.zh: 你知道，华盛顿大游行是锦上添花，在数十年的立法行动和战略性的静坐之后。
